definition: An assessment of climate or disaster risk to infrastructure or facilities that this project itself carries out, finances or requires: a site-specific assessment of the works and sites it finances, a sector-wide or national assessment of existing infrastructure, an assessment that operators, contractors or bidders must carry out, or hazard and risk mapping used to decide where infrastructure goes. Hazards include floods, storms and cyclones, sea level rise, heat, drought, landslides and earthquakes. The World Bank's own climate and disaster risk screening of the project at appraisal, and a statement that the project was screened or is aligned with the Paris Agreement, are not this: they are the Bank's work, done before the project, not something the project commits to.
note: Deliberately silent on digital assets: the asset link is computed separately (the asset map), because the decision model reads a question literally and does not infer that a tower is digital infrastructure. v2 (2026-10-19): the Bank's appraisal-stage screening excluded; on the first graded sheet every false positive was that screening.
